title.narrative: Output 6.3. Increased capacity of Member States to develop gender-responsive legislation, policies and measures for a world of work free from violence and harassment

description.narrative:
1. For implementing the revised 2019 Labour Code and subsequent decree no. 145 and in alignment with Convention No.190, in particular on the provisions of prevention of sexual harassment at work, the MOLISA in collaboration with Social Partners, line ministry, and ILO developed a new Code of Conduct. This Code of Conduct has been adopted by tripartite constituents, and submitted for final endorsement to the National IR Council.
A Handbook guiding employers on implementing the new Code of Conduct on sexual harassment has already been developed, piloted, and updated, and is being rolled out further until the end of the year in two sectors. The Handbook will be used as training materials by the MOLISA and Social Partners. 1. ILO (at HQ, Regional, and Country levels) provided significant technical comments and inputs during the development, piloting, and finalization of the handbook. 2. ILO is a core member of the national technical working group that provided inputs for the development and finalization of the CoC. 3. ILO developed and disseminated the communication materials on the promotion of C.190

description.narrative: MOLISA submitted a proposed dossier to revise the 2013 Employment Law to the National Assembly in February 2023, which in June 2023 it was approved to be included in the formal law-making plan of the National Assembly for 2024. Important proposals for revision include detailed provisions of sector skills council, informal employment protection, more provisions of employment for people with disability, improvised labour market information system. ILO’s support to the development of a dossier to propose for the revision of the 2013 Employment Law was delivered as of February 2022 and is ongoing. The dossier presents itself as a required package of documents for requesting the revision of the previous 2013 Employment Law. ILO provided detailed technical comments to the report on the implementation of the 2013 Employment Law and gave suggestions for the new outline of the revised Employment Law. ILO also helped to make available national expertise for the development of impact assessment reports that form the foundation of the dossier. The revision aims at highlighting employment as both the objective and also as a cross-cutting component of socio-economic policies, contributing to enhancing productive employment in Viet Nam. The whole package of comments was shared with MOLISA on 7th October 2022. The dossier was submitted by the Government to National Assembly in February 2023 and approved in June 2023 to be included in the formal law-making plan of the National Assembly for 2024. Some suggestions from the ILO have been reflected in the dossier such as sector skills council, informal employment, employment for people with disability, labour market information system. MOLISA requested ILO’s continued support to the employment law revision process. The next stage of support will run from July 2023 to October 2024 when the first draft revised law is submitted for the National Assembly’s review. ILO will continue working with the drafting team on the development of provisions/articles aiming at making the Employment Law in line with international labour standards and regulations. Special focus of ILO’s support included gender, skills certification, employment services, informal employment, unemployment insurance, and credits for job creation.
